# process_manager

In [EhOsContract.Contract](contract-dsl.md), section `contract`.

```elixir
process_manager name, label
```

Steers a run: starts on an event, reacts, sets timers, ends.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="contract-process_manager-name"></a>`name` | `atom` | yes |  | The process manager's name. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-label"></a>`label` | `String.t` | yes |  | What it steers, as the business says it. |

**Options**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="contract-process_manager-correlate"></a>`correlate` | `atom \| list(atom)` | yes |  | The fields that tell which run an event belongs to. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-delivery"></a>`delivery` | `:in_transaction \| :at_least_once` |  | `:at_least_once` | When it runs. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-idempotency"></a>`idempotency` | `[key: atom, owner: :self \| :downstream \| :infrastructure]` |  |  | What makes a second delivery harmless, and who keeps it so: `[key: :event_id, owner: :self]`. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-source"></a>`source` | `String.t` |  |  | Where the process manager comes from in the material. |

Inside it: [`state`](#contract-process_manager-state), [`starts_on`](#contract-process_manager-starts_on), [`on`](#contract-process_manager-on), [`timer`](#contract-process_manager-timer), [`ends_on`](#contract-process_manager-ends_on), [`invariant`](#contract-process_manager-invariant), [`constraint`](#contract-process_manager-constraint).

## process_manager.timer

```elixir
timer name, label
```

A timer of a process manager: after a wait, or at a time in its state.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="contract-process_manager-timer-name"></a>`name` | `atom` | yes |  | The timer's name. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-timer-label"></a>`label` | `String.t` | yes |  | What the timer is for, as the business says it; `wait:` or `at:` says when. |

**Options**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="contract-process_manager-timer-wait"></a>`wait` | `any` |  |  | How long after it is set it fires, `{n, unit}`. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-timer-at"></a>`at` | `atom` |  |  | The `:timestamp` field of the state it fires at. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-timer-issues"></a>`issues` | `atom \| list(atom)` |  | `[]` | Commands it issues when it fires. |
| <a id="contract-process_manager-timer-source"></a>`source` | `String.t` |  |  | Where the timer comes from in the material. |
